origin.description: Count the bytes used to store each string.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

origin.details: For UTF-8, one code point may take 1 to 4 bytes, so this can be larger than stri_length. The trailing NUL that C uses to end a string is not included. A missing string stays missing.
origin.value: An integer vector the same length as str.

translation.description: Count the UTF-8 bytes used to store each string.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, a number, a complex value, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

translation.details: The byte count is the UTF-8 encoding of the coerced string. It does not include a trailing NUL. U+0105 is one code point and two bytes. NA stays missing.
translation.value: An int, or NA. A list or tuple returns a list. None returns an empty list.
translation.example:
from stringi.length import stri_numbytes
print(f"stri_numbytes(\"\\u0105\") returns {stri_numbytes(chr(0x105))}.")
